core_obligations: The setup (proof lines 1027-1035): an extension problem for an abelian sheaf along a subsheaf of a standard object is considered, and the author aims to enlarge the domain of a given partial extension step by step.

Enlarging the domain (proof lines 1036-1052): for a morphism from the standard object to the target, the intersection of its image with the current domain is cut out and the restriction of the given morphism to that intersection is studied, which produces a morphism on the image of the standard object agreeing with the given one on the intersection.

Gluing (proof lines 1052-1055): the two morphisms glue by the sheaf axioms to give an extension to the strictly larger subsheaf obtained by adding the image, so the extension process can be iterated and terminates, which gives the extension property and hence injectivity.
proof_roadmap: Formulate an extension problem along a subsheaf of a standard object.
Add the image of one morphism from a standard object to the domain, using that the restrictions agree on the intersection.
Glue by the sheaf axioms and iterate, which yields the injectivity criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a sheaf of abelian groups to be injective, namely that morphisms out of subsheaves of the standard objects always extend (statement lines 1017-1025). The proof is a complete argument: starting from an extension problem, the author enlarges the domain by adding the image of a morphism from a standard object, computing the restriction on the intersection of the two subsheaves (proof lines 1027-1052) and gluing the two morphisms there by the sheaf axioms to obtain an extension to a strictly larger subsheaf (proof lines 1052-1055), so that the process terminates and the extension property, hence injectivity, follows. The non-formal content is the gluing step. The claim is H2.
